whys.compose.default: The chain darkens the plate slightly for contrast against the misty wet concrete, tints the type from the footage's sunrise orange, and sandwiches it behind the rider so the subject stays solid in front.
whys.idea: The footage already tracks the rider through mist and wet concrete, and the post-rock build at 90 bpm wants weight that the subject can push through, so putting the type behind the rider makes the words feel carved into the world the skater is moving through.
whys.system: The post-rock swells need one strong, consistent voice; thinning the weight across the five words mirrors the slow build and release of the music while the constant lanes module and behind placement keep the eye on the rider.
whys.word[0] FIRST: Heavy Anybody at full weight opens the piece on the first downbeat (0.36s); lanes form-in draws the outline from the wet concrete, and flat render keeps it crisp against the busy misty bowl.
whys.word[1] LIGHT: Hit on the 2.36s downbeat as the shot cuts to the carve; slightly thinner weight and a ripple transition answer the mist spray rising off the lip.
whys.word[2] CARVE: Hit on the 5.03s chord change into harmony 2; the fan transition and the word's own shot (concrete-formed letters) make the type feel part of the ramp as the rider drifts.
whys.word[3] DRIFT: Hit on the 7.7s chord change as the rider stops and looks back; the twist transition matches the slow push-in camera and the settling mist.
whys.word[4] HOLD: Hit on the 10.36s chord change into harmony 4; drops to tall condensed Big Shoulders Display so the final word is lighter and calmer, clearing before the 16s fade.

compose.cuts.why: The rider is moving laterally right in s1, so the shards slide right into the carve shot; the cut lands on the 2.36s downbeat.
The music builds into the 5.03s chord change, so the camera dives into the carve shot and arrives at the drift.
Both shots have a clear subject and matte; the pivot on the 7.7s chord change keeps the rider crisp in front while the background transforms.
The rider stops and the music releases at 10.36s, so the camera backs out and the HOLD shot flies in past the lens.
s6 continues the same place and camera drift, so a hard cut on the 13.03s chord change keeps the flow unbroken into the final hold.
